entities.summary: The Temple of Jupiter Feretrius was, according to legend, the first temple ever built in Rome. Its site is uncertain but is thought to have been on the Capitoline Hill. According to Roman legend, the temple was dedicated by Romulus as a shrine for spolia opima, armor taken from an enemy commander whom a Roman had killed in single combat. Counting Romulus's own contribution, three such offerings were said to have been made in the regal and republican periods, during which the temple was also a center of activity for the Fetial priesthood.
